preparation.missing: If the inventory is incomplete, the proposed structure remains provisional. The skill can propose a sitemap, but card sorts, tree tests and real user results require actual research rather than a generated claim of validation.

build-interactive-proposal.what: Build a page for exploring scope options.
build-interactive-proposal.when: A priced proposal or an unpriced scope explorer is needed.
build-interactive-proposal.inputs: Versioned scope, options, assumptions, and confirmed prices when applicable.
build-interactive-proposal.outputs: An interactive HTML page with selectable options and reconciled figures.
build-interactive-proposal.example: Create an interactive comparison of these scope options using the confirmed quote figures.
build-interactive-proposal.expect: It announces whether it is in Proposal mode (a priced quote exists) or Explorer mode (no quote, so no currency anywhere) and builds one self-contained HTML page. A source mismatch or unsupported fee blocks the build, and the page is not deliverable until parity, visual and prose checks each have a written result.
build-interactive-proposal.requires: Needs a quote export or source documents, and Python 3 for the builder; browser checks also need Node.js, Playwright and Chromium.
build-interactive-proposal.overview: It announces whether it is in Proposal mode (a priced quote exists) or Explorer mode (no quote, so no currency anywhere) and builds one self-contained HTML page. A source mismatch or unsupported fee blocks the build, and the page is not deliverable until parity, visual and prose checks each have a written result.
build-interactive-proposal.value: Let a buyer inspect scope options and their consequences in one interactive page. It keeps inclusions, assumptions and confirmed figures connected as options are selected.

preparation.where: Provide versioned scope and option data. A dated quote export supports priced Proposal mode; source documents without a quote support unpriced Explorer mode. A live quote connector is unnecessary if you supply the required export.
preparation.missing: Without a quote it uses Explorer mode with no currency. Unsupported fees or mismatched scope figures block a priced build. Browser checks require the documented runtime; an untested render cannot be described as visually checked.

map-journey.what: Map a customer or role’s experience and the service underneath.
map-journey.when: A journey map, service blueprint, or opportunity map is needed.
map-journey.inputs: Touchpoints, research, goals, friction, roles, and system evidence.
map-journey.outputs: A journey or blueprint with sourced findings and labeled hypotheses.
map-journey.example: Map this customer journey from research through the service and systems underneath.
map-journey.expect: It confirms the actor, the starting and ending events and the decision first, then produces a journey map, a service blueprint and an opportunity map that share one set of phases. Each claim names its source or is labeled as a hypothesis, and a release check it cannot run is reported as missing instead of passed.
map-journey.requires: Needs a named actor and journey plus sources such as transcripts, tickets, analytics or system records; without interviews it can only draft the human layers as labeled hypotheses.
map-journey.overview: It confirms the actor, the starting and ending events and the decision first, then produces a journey map, a service blueprint and an opportunity map that share one set of phases. Each claim names its source or is labeled as a hypothesis, and a release check it cannot run is reported as missing instead of passed.
map-journey.value: Connect a person's experience to the people, processes and systems delivering it. The journey map, service blueprint and opportunity map share phases so a visible customer problem can be traced to its operational cause.

preparation.where: Name the actor, start and end events, and decision the map should support. Bring interviews, tickets, analytics or system records. A service blueprint is the behind-the-scenes view the skill creates; you do not need one already.
preparation.missing: Without interviews, human goals, thoughts and emotions can only be labeled hypotheses. Missing system evidence stays open. Research supplies factual observations; the skill does not create evidence by drawing a plausible journey.

frame-jobs-to-be-done.what: Frame the job a person is trying to accomplish and test whether the framing changes a decision.
frame-jobs-to-be-done.when: Job statements, struggling moments, hire and fire criteria, or an audit of existing JTBD work are needed.
frame-jobs-to-be-done.inputs: Research about recent struggling moments and switch decisions, or a request for hypotheses with interview prompts when none exists.
frame-jobs-to-be-done.outputs: Job framing with evidence references, decision implications, remaining research questions and an audit against twelve checks.
frame-jobs-to-be-done.example: Extract the struggling moments and hire criteria from these interviews before drafting job statements.
frame-jobs-to-be-done.expect: It works from struggling moments and hire and fire criteria in the research you supply, and writes job statements only where the source shows the outcome. With no research it produces hypotheses marked as such plus interview prompts, and it will say when the framing only restates a feature list.
frame-jobs-to-be-done.requires: Needs interview or switch-decision research to state factual jobs; without it the output is limited to labeled hypotheses and interview prompts.
frame-jobs-to-be-done.overview: It works from struggling moments and hire and fire criteria in the research you supply, and writes job statements only where the source shows the outcome. With no research it produces hypotheses marked as such plus interview prompts, and it will say when the framing only restates a feature list.
frame-jobs-to-be-done.value: Explain the outcome someone is trying to achieve and why they would change solutions. It helps a team choose between solving a real struggle and merely restating a feature request.

preparation.where: Bring accounts of recent struggling moments or switch decisions, ideally interview excerpts showing the situation, desired progress and hiring/firing criteria. Those criteria describe why a person adopts or abandons a solution; they are research inputs, not another installed skill.
preparation.missing: With no research, it can produce labeled job hypotheses and interview prompts. It cannot call those hypotheses factual jobs or invent a customer's motives; evidence is needed before using them as confirmed findings.

manage-consulting-knowledge.what: Retrieve and maintain a project’s durable knowledge.
manage-consulting-knowledge.when: Work needs current client, pursuit, engagement, or evidence records.
manage-consulting-knowledge.inputs: The confirmed project identity, permitted storage, and relevant sources.
manage-consulting-knowledge.outputs: Retrieved context or verified workspace and record updates.
manage-consulting-knowledge.example: Find the current discovery and decision records for this opportunity in the permitted store.
manage-consulting-knowledge.expect: It confirms the client and the opportunity or engagement first and stops if identity is ambiguous, then reads the front door and only the records the task needs. Writes go to the declared primary store only, with a hash check, and it reports one of five persistence states, so a returned patch is never described as an update.
manage-consulting-knowledge.requires: Needs a hub folder, a Google Drive hub or supplied files, and Python 3 to run the record and workspace scripts.
manage-consulting-knowledge.overview: It confirms the client and the opportunity or engagement first and stops if identity is ambiguous, then reads the front door and only the records the task needs. Writes go to the declared primary store only, with a hash check, and it reports one of five persistence states, so a returned patch is never described as an update.
manage-consulting-knowledge.value: Find and maintain the project records that later work should use: client context, opportunity findings, engagement decisions and evidence. It helps avoid conflicting copies and updates written to the wrong deal or client.

preparation.where: Identify the client and opportunity or engagement, then provide the project folder, supported Drive hub or supplied files. A front door is the index pointing to current records. The primary store is the destination your project has selected for updates.
preparation.missing: Ambiguous client identity stops retrieval or writes to prevent filing under the wrong record. With supplied files it can work locally; persistent updates require a declared writable destination and a verified result.

apply-author-style.what: Apply an explicitly selected author’s confirmed writing profile.
apply-author-style.when: The task names an author and provides or authorizes their profile.
apply-author-style.inputs: The draft, sources, intended author and confirmed profile.
apply-author-style.outputs: Complete prose preserving supported claims and confirmed author preferences.
apply-author-style.example: Rewrite this About draft in my voice while preserving its supported claims.
apply-author-style.reuseNote: Use the caller’s explicitly supplied or authorized sources, configuration, profile and destination. No personal identity or standing permissions transfer with the workflow.
apply-author-style.expect: It uses a writing profile only when one for the named author is supplied or authorized for the task, and reads the profile's ownership and revocation state first. With no profile it falls back to plain drafting, and it will not claim a profile was loaded or a scan was run when it was not.
apply-author-style.requires: A confirmed author writing profile supplied in the task or held in an authorized private profile store.
apply-author-style.overview: It uses a writing profile only when one for the named author is supplied or authorized for the task, and reads the profile's ownership and revocation state first. With no profile it falls back to plain drafting, and it will not claim a profile was loaded or a scan was run when it was not.
apply-author-style.value: Use an authorized author's actual preferences while preserving the draft's claims and meaning. It is useful for personal copy where a generic house voice would misrepresent the writer.

preparation.where: Provide the draft, intended author and a writing profile explicitly authorized for this task. A profile is a private record of confirmed style preferences and its allowed uses; having an email connector does not authorize constructing one.
preparation.missing: Without an authorized profile, it can draft plainly but cannot claim to match a learned voice. Use Manage writing profile only if you want to build a profile from samples you authorize; it is not required for ordinary editing.

preparationSkills.reason: Optional preparation when you want a new profile from authorized writing samples.

verify-salesforce-org.what: Verify the Salesforce organization before a write.
verify-salesforce-org.when: A Salesforce record change, upload, or deployment is about to occur.
verify-salesforce-org.inputs: The intended org ID, sandbox status, connection, and requested action.
verify-salesforce-org.outputs: A current identity check and a proceed or stop decision.
verify-salesforce-org.example: Verify the intended Salesforce org ID and sandbox status before this record update.
verify-salesforce-org.expect: It queries the Organization record on the named connection and compares the org ID and sandbox flag with the intended target. It refuses a missing, unknown, mismatched or malformed identity, requires an explicit flag for production, and a pass does not authorize the deployment.
verify-salesforce-org.overview: It queries the Organization record on the named connection and compares the org ID and sandbox flag with the intended target. It refuses a missing, unknown, mismatched or malformed identity, requires an explicit flag for production, and a pass does not authorize the deployment.
verify-salesforce-org.value: Confirm the Salesforce org connected to a write before the operation runs. Comparing the actual org ID and sandbox flag helps catch an alias pointing at the wrong environment.

preparation.where: Provide the intended org ID, whether it is a sandbox and the selected authenticated connection. The authoritative identity comes from querying Salesforce's Organization record, not from trusting a local alias name.
preparation.missing: A missing, unknown or mismatched identity blocks the write. Without login access this check cannot complete. A correct identity check does not itself authorize a production action.

author-style-runtime.what: Apply one person’s confirmed writing profile.
author-style-runtime.when: The intended author has an approved private style profile.
author-style-runtime.inputs: That author’s profile, its scope, and a configured installation adapter.
author-style-runtime.outputs: Writing reviewed against the selected author’s profile.
author-style-runtime.example: Apply the confirmed author profile to this draft within its stated scope.
author-style-runtime.expect: It first decides who the author is, plus the surface, audience and purpose, and applies a confirmed profile only when the profiled person is the author. It falls back to plain drafting when the profile has no confirmed entry for that case, and never applies it to quotations or organizational voice.
author-style-runtime.overview: It first decides who the author is, plus the surface, audience and purpose, and applies a confirmed profile only when the profiled person is the author. It falls back to plain drafting when the profile has no confirmed entry for that case, and never applies it to quotations or organizational voice.
author-style-runtime.value: Apply the right parts of a confirmed writing profile to the actual author, audience and surface. It is a shared helper for profile-aware writing, rather than a second independent editing workflow.

preparation.where: The calling skill supplies author identity, task context and an authorized private profile through its installation adapter. The adapter connects the workflow to the chosen profile store; it must be configured for that environment.
preparation.missing: If there is no confirmed profile entry for the situation, use plain drafting. Quoted text and organizational voice do not inherit a person's profile. This runtime is included by its callers; you normally select Apply author style instead.

manage-service-offering.what: Define and maintain a productized service offering.
manage-service-offering.when: An offering needs definition, comparison, or catalog maintenance.
manage-service-offering.inputs: The buyer, problem, proposed service, scope, and current catalog.
manage-service-offering.outputs: A structured offering with value, deliverables, boundaries, and catalog decisions.
manage-service-offering.example: Define the buyer, value, deliverables, and boundaries for this service offering.
manage-service-offering.expect: It works out which job you want (define, audit, deduplicate, add or replace, maintain), then answers the seven Clarity questions before rendering anything in the house format. It will not invent prices, durations or figures, lists open choices as decisions to lock, and checks that untouched catalog entries stayed byte-identical.
manage-service-offering.requires: Needs the existing catalog file when editing one, and Python 3 for the corpus verifier.
manage-service-offering.overview: It works out which job you want (define, audit, deduplicate, add or replace, maintain), then answers the seven Clarity questions before rendering anything in the house format. It will not invent prices, durations or figures, lists open choices as decisions to lock, and checks that untouched catalog entries stayed byte-identical.
manage-service-offering.value: Turn a service idea into an offering someone can assess and deliver: a defined buyer, problem, value, scope and boundaries. It also audits or deduplicates an existing offering catalog without rewriting unrelated entries.

preparation.where: For a new offering, provide the buyer, problem and proposed service. For catalog changes, supply the actual current catalog file. The Clarity questions are the framework in this skill; they do not require another service or account.
preparation.missing: Unknown prices, durations and metrics remain decisions to confirm. Without the current catalog it cannot verify an edit or deduplication against existing entries; a new offering can still be developed from your brief.

assess-offering-fit.what: Match a prospect’s needs to an offering.
assess-offering-fit.when: Discovery needs to become an assess-offering-fit decision.
assess-offering-fit.inputs: The current offering catalog and supported prospect findings.
assess-offering-fit.outputs: Ranked fit, evidence behind the score, disqualifiers, and open questions.
assess-offering-fit.example: Compare this prospect’s discovery findings with our current offering catalog.
assess-offering-fit.expect: It reads the discovery material and scores signals against each playbook's qualifier, citing the source of every point. It returns a ranked top three with the unanswered gates as the next call's agenda, does not price or lock a tier, and treats a run without the approved qualifier schema as diagnostic only.
assess-offering-fit.overview: It reads the discovery material and scores signals against each playbook's qualifier, citing the source of every point. It returns a ranked top three with the unanswered gates as the next call's agenda, does not price or lock a tier, and treats a run without the approved qualifier schema as diagnostic only.
assess-offering-fit.value: Compare a prospect's supported needs with an existing service catalog. It shows which offerings fit, which gates remain unanswered and what the next call should establish before anyone commits a tier or price.

preparation.where: Supply discovery findings and the offering catalog with its qualifiers. A qualifier schema defines the fields and scoring rules your organization approves for judging fit; it is catalog configuration, not a universally supplied scoring model.
preparation.missing: Without the approved qualifier schema the assessment is diagnostic only. Missing discovery evidence becomes a question, not a scored fact. It does not create a new offering or price one to fill a catalog gap.

render-offering-brief.what: Render an offering into sales handouts.
render-offering-brief.when: A defined offering needs internal enablement or an external handout.
render-offering-brief.inputs: Structured offering content and the selected brand profile.
render-offering-brief.outputs: A two-page internal brief and one-page external PDF, checked after rendering.
render-offering-brief.example: Render this defined offering as an internal brief and an external handout.
render-offering-brief.expect: It renders one playbook into a two-page internal brief and a one-page external PDF from structured Markdown or a JSON spec, using the confirmed brand profile or the neutral one. It adds no claims to fill a slot, fails on missing content, overflow or a wrong page count, and keeps failed attempts instead of overwriting them.
render-offering-brief.requires: Needs Python 3 with Jinja2 and pypdf, plus Node.js, Playwright and Chromium installed locally through the setup steps in the instructions.
render-offering-brief.overview: It turns one structured offering definition into a two-page internal brief and a one-page external PDF. It applies the confirmed brand or neutral profile, checks that required content is present, and checks rendered page counts and overflow. It does not add claims or figures to fill the available space.
render-offering-brief.value: Give sales and delivery a concise handout from the same approved offering definition. It produces an internal explanation and an external version while checking that the content fits the intended page counts.

preparation.where: Provide structured offering Markdown or a JSON specification and the selected brand profile. Manage service offering can produce the definition; an equivalent complete definition can be supplied directly. The renderer needs the Python and browser libraries listed in its setup instructions.
preparation.missing: Missing required content or overflow fails the render; the skill does not add claims to fill empty slots. Without the runtime it cannot produce and inspect the PDFs. No custom brand is required when neutral defaults are appropriate.

preparationSkills.reason: Develops the structured offering definition; an equivalent supplied definition also works.

plan-offering-artifacts.what: Plan and track the artifacts for an offering.
plan-offering-artifacts.when: An offering needs a complete artifact package or readiness review.
plan-offering-artifacts.inputs: The offering definition, manifest, existing artifacts, and commercial policy.
plan-offering-artifacts.outputs: An artifact plan, owning workflows, and remaining readiness checks.
plan-offering-artifacts.example: Review this offering’s artifact manifest and identify what remains before release.
plan-offering-artifacts.expect: It runs a planner against the playbook's manifest and reports the ordered build plan with every finding, then works one ready artifact at a time. Nothing is marked complete without three written gate results, and because the approved specification is supplied by the caller its output says release readiness is unverified.
plan-offering-artifacts.overview: It runs a planner against the playbook's manifest and reports the ordered build plan with every finding, then works one ready artifact at a time. Nothing is marked complete without three written gate results, and because the approved specification is supplied by the caller its output says release readiness is unverified.
plan-offering-artifacts.value: Show which pieces of an offering package exist, which are blocked and which workflow should produce the next one. It helps prevent an attractive sales handout from masking missing commercial or delivery material.

preparation.where: Supply the offering definition, artifact manifest and your approved specification, qualifier schemas and stage-gate workbook. The manifest lists required deliverables and their states; the external specification defines what your organization accepts.
preparation.missing: Without those external rules, the bundled compatibility checks cannot certify readiness. It can identify missing records and an ordered plan, but cannot mark an offering release-ready by treating its own templates as your approval policy.

write-feature-spec.when: A feature needs a PRD, development brief, or acceptance criteria.
write-feature-spec.inputs: The problem, users, evidence, constraints, and requested scope.
write-feature-spec.outputs: A specification with behavior, requirements, and testable acceptance criteria.
write-feature-spec.example: Write a feature specification with user behavior, requirements, and acceptance criteria.
write-feature-spec.expect: It reads the brief, sources and existing decisions first, then drafts a spec at the depth the change needs with observable acceptance criteria. It asks only about a decision that blocks useful work, drafts the supported parts meanwhile, and will not invent a baseline, estimate, date or owner.
write-feature-spec.overview: It reads the brief, sources and existing decisions first, then drafts a spec at the depth the change needs with observable acceptance criteria. It asks only about a decision that blocks useful work, drafts the supported parts meanwhile, and will not invent a baseline, estimate, date or owner.
write-feature-spec.value: Translate a product problem into behavior engineers can build and testers can observe. It connects user flows, requirements and acceptance criteria so scope decisions do not remain hidden in a broad feature description.

preparation.where: Supply the problem, intended users, evidence and constraints. Existing decisions may be in a brief, design file, repository or notes; no formal PRD is required before asking the skill to write one.
preparation.missing: It drafts supported sections while asking about decisions that block useful progress. Missing baseline figures, owners or dates stay unresolved. For a deeper implementation contract, its detailed specification mode adds UI, API, data and affected-file detail.

preparationSkills.reason: Provides deeper UI, API, data and affected-file detail when the feature needs it.

prioritize-work.what: Rank candidates with a named framework and check the evidence behind each score.
prioritize-work.when: A team must choose between problems, outcomes, roadmap candidates or backlog items.
prioritize-work.inputs: Candidates with their scoring inputs and the source for each input.
prioritize-work.outputs: A ranked proposal with each item's formula, flagged unsourced inputs and ties, and the decision owner named.
prioritize-work.example: RICE-score these eight roadmap candidates and flag any score that rests on a guess.
prioritize-work.expect: It names what is being ranked and picks one framework with a stated reason, then collects each score input with a source and runs a scoring script. The output is a ranked proposal with formulas, flags and a named decision owner, and the flags are carried forward, not cleared by raising a number.
prioritize-work.requires: Needs a candidate list with sourced inputs for the chosen framework and Python 3 for the scoring script.
prioritize-work.overview: It names what is being ranked and picks one framework with a stated reason, then collects each score input with a source and runs a scoring script. The output is a ranked proposal with formulas, flags and a named decision owner, and the flags are carried forward, not cleared by raising a number.
prioritize-work.value: Make a ranking inspectable instead of presenting an unexplained score. It shows the formula, source inputs, ties and uncertainties behind candidate priorities so the decision owner can challenge the trade-offs.

preparation.where: Provide the items to rank and evidence for the chosen framework, such as reach, impact, confidence and effort for RICE. These values come from research, analytics and team estimates; the skill supplies the scoring method, not the measurements.
preparation.missing: Missing inputs stay flagged rather than being raised to improve a candidate's rank. The result is a prioritization proposal, not an authorized tracker update. A score cannot resolve a decision whose evidence is still absent.

design-process.what: Document a process or identify improvements.
design-process.when: An SOP, ownership map, or process optimization is needed.
design-process.inputs: The current steps, roles, exceptions, constraints, and available measures.
design-process.outputs: An SOP or improvement analysis covering time, cost, quality, and ownership.
design-process.example: Document this approval process as an SOP with owners, exceptions, and measures.
design-process.expect: It picks Document mode (an SOP with a RACI) or Optimize mode from your request, and asks targeted questions when the description is thin. It writes not captured or open: for missing owners, durations and figures, and will not invent an impact estimate.
design-process.overview: It picks Document mode (an SOP with a RACI) or Optimize mode from your request, and asks targeted questions when the description is thin. It writes not captured or open: for missing owners, durations and figures, and will not invent an impact estimate.
design-process.value: Make a repeatable business process explicit, or identify where it loses time, money or quality. It separates an SOP for doing the work from an improvement analysis of how that work could change.

preparation.where: Describe the current steps, roles, handoffs, exceptions and available measurements. An SOP is the operating procedure this workflow creates. RACI names who is responsible, accountable, consulted and informed; it is an output table rather than a separate prerequisite skill.
preparation.missing: If the description is thin, begin with targeted questions. Unknown owners, durations and figures remain open. Optimization can identify likely issues but cannot claim quantified savings without a measurement basis.

develop-product.what: Develop a product from its current evidence and release state.
develop-product.when: Starting or resuming a product at a requested stage.
develop-product.inputs: The product brief, current sources, decisions, and readiness evidence.
develop-product.outputs: An updated product record and the next supported development action.
develop-product.example: Resume this product at its current stage using the recorded readiness evidence.
develop-product.expect: It enters at the stage you request, reuses the existing product home and decisions, and keeps source review, product decision and implementation evidence as separate states. It records readiness gates for the stage, names the next action with its required authorization, and never reports proposed or local work as released or live.
develop-product.requires: Needs an existing product home or an authorized place to create one, plus the supplied source material for the stage.
develop-product.overview: It enters at the stage you request, reuses the existing product home and decisions, and keeps source review, product decision and implementation evidence as separate states. It records readiness gates for the stage, names the next action with its required authorization, and never reports proposed or local work as released or live.
develop-product.value: Resume product work at the stage it actually reached and identify the next justified decision or delivery action. It is useful when research, product definition and implementation evidence have become disconnected across sessions.

preparation.where: Point to the product's existing folder or record and state the stage or result you want. A product home is simply its agreed location for briefs, evidence, decisions and release records; the workflow can use an authorized new location when starting from scratch.
preparation.missing: Without readiness evidence it cannot declare a stage complete. It can organize the supplied material and name the missing decision. A standalone bug or specification does not need the whole product-development pathway.

writing-diagnostics.what: Run the writing diagnostics and figure checks that review-writing uses.
writing-diagnostics.when: Writing-integrity needs a pattern scan, a figure tie-out or a review receipt.
writing-diagnostics.inputs: The saved text, the source version for figure comparison and the house configuration.
writing-diagnostics.outputs: Pattern findings, figure comparisons and validated review receipts; it does not rewrite text.
writing-diagnostics.example: Check this saved draft for recurring writing patterns and confirm no figure changed from the source.
writing-diagnostics.expect: It is an internal checker used by the writing review, not an editor, and it reports detectable patterns in a saved file by exit code without rewriting anything. It can reconcile figures between a source and a rewrite and emit a review receipt, but a clean scan does not show the prose was read.
writing-diagnostics.requires: Needs Python 3 and a saved file to check.
writing-diagnostics.overview: It scans saved text for detectable writing patterns, compares figures between source and revised versions, and validates review receipts. The scripts return findings and exit codes; they do not rewrite the draft or select an author voice. A human or writing-review workflow still has to read the prose and judge whether a finding applies.
writing-diagnostics.value: Find detectable writing patterns and compare figures between a source and a rewrite. It supports editing with specific findings and receipts, while leaving meaning and editorial decisions to the writing review.

preparation.where: Supply a saved text or supported document. A source version is needed only for figure comparison; a review receipt is a generated record of the checks and assessment. Python runs the bundled scripts without a neighboring skill installation.
preparation.missing: Without a saved file the scanner cannot run. Without the source version it cannot verify figure preservation. You can use Review writing for an edit; a clean diagnostic result alone does not establish good prose or factual accuracy.

preparationSkills.reason: Owns the editorial review that interprets these scanner findings.

review-deliverable.what: Review a finished artifact against the request and sources.
review-deliverable.when: A material deliverable is approaching release.
review-deliverable.inputs: The artifact, controlling sources, output requirements, and actual checks.
review-deliverable.outputs: A release decision with supported findings and required repairs.
review-deliverable.example: Review this deliverable against its sources, requested outcome, and rendered form.
review-deliverable.expect: It opens the finished artifact and its sources, then records each required check as pass, fail, blocked or not applicable with cited evidence. A missing prose receipt, brand report or source for a claim blocks release, and it returns a remediation list instead of marking anything complete.
review-deliverable.requires: Needs the finished artifact and its evidence record, and Python 3 to run the quality record validator.
review-deliverable.overview: It opens the finished artifact and its sources, then records each required check as pass, fail, blocked or not applicable with cited evidence. A missing prose receipt, brand report or source for a claim blocks release, and it returns a remediation list instead of marking anything complete.
review-deliverable.value: Decide whether a finished artifact meets its request, sources, format and release requirements. It gives repairs tied to evidence rather than a general impression that the output looks polished.

preparation.where: Provide the actual finished artifact, original brief, controlling sources and the checks its producing workflow requires. Evidence records are the receipts or results of those checks; they are not supplied by this review automatically.
preparation.missing: Missing required sources or checks are recorded as blocked. The review can identify what must be repaired or obtained, but cannot create approval evidence or mark an unperformed render inspection as passed.

capture-requirements.what: Turn source material into a structured requirements backlog through a guided conversation.
capture-requirements.when: Requirements, user stories or a SOW-to-backlog workbook are needed.
capture-requirements.inputs: The brief, SOW, transcripts or product sources, and confirmation of the proposed hierarchy.
capture-requirements.outputs: A two-tab Excel workbook of epics, capabilities, business needs, stories, Gherkin acceptance criteria and MoSCoW priorities.
capture-requirements.example: Turn this SOW into a requirements workbook with stories and testable acceptance criteria.
capture-requirements.expect: It starts with a conversation, not a file: it reads your source material, proposes the epic hierarchy and asks you to confirm it before generating anything. It then builds a two-tab Excel workbook with Gherkin acceptance criteria and MoSCoW priorities, defaults unclear priority to Must Have with flagged assumptions, and keeps versioned copies as you revise.
capture-requirements.requires: Needs source material (deck, PRD, brief or transcript, or a Salesforce SOW in BA mode) and a spreadsheet skill with a recalculation script available to build the workbook.
capture-requirements.overview: It reads your brief, SOW or other sources and works with you to confirm an epic hierarchy before generating a backlog. It builds a two-tab Excel workbook linking epics, capabilities, business needs and stories to Gherkin acceptance criteria and MoSCoW priorities. Ambiguous priorities and unsupported detail remain visible for review rather than becoming silent commitments.
capture-requirements.value: Turn source documents into an organized backlog that a team can discuss and test. It proposes the hierarchy with you before writing stories, acceptance criteria and priorities into a workbook.

preparation.where: Bring a brief, SOW, deck, PRD or transcript. The hierarchy groups epics, capabilities, business needs and stories; the workflow proposes it, so you need not prebuild a backlog. A spreadsheet tool with recalculation support is needed for the Excel output.
preparation.missing: You can start from source material and confirm the proposed hierarchy in conversation. Unsupported details remain assumptions or questions. Without spreadsheet capability the required workbook cannot be built and verified as complete.

preparationSkills.reason: Checks the completed stories for readiness before sprint planning.

tailor-resume.what: Apply the user’s resume methods for figures and ATS wording.
tailor-resume.when: A tailored resume needs supported quantified bullets or role-relevant keyword placement.
tailor-resume.inputs: Current career evidence, the posting, and the draft resume.
tailor-resume.outputs: Revised bullets and layout that preserve the user’s stated scope and evidence.
tailor-resume.example: Review my resume bullets against this posting and the current source figures.
tailor-resume.reuseNote: Use the caller’s explicitly supplied or authorized sources, configuration, profile and destination. No personal identity or standing permissions transfer with the workflow.
tailor-resume.expect: It starts with the posting and selected evidence, checks claims against corrections, original sources and the ledger, then writes the relevant résumé copy. Keywords and platform names appear where they explain supported work, without numerical quotas or a required leadership or client example.
tailor-resume.requires: Needs the candidate's confirmed career records (operating context, role work record, master resume and evidence ledger) and the live posting or its saved snapshot.
tailor-resume.overview: It starts with the posting and selected evidence, checks claims against corrections, original sources and the ledger, then writes the relevant résumé copy. Keywords and platform names appear where they explain supported work, without numerical quotas or a required leadership or client example.
tailor-resume.value: Translate relevant experience into accurate hiring copy without forcing a repeated theme or adding unsupported ownership.

preparation.where: Supply the master resume, posting and role work record. The translation table maps role requirements to specific experience; career claim records hold the underlying figures and ownership. These are your evidence documents, not built-in personal history.
preparation.missing: An empty translation table stops this wording step. Prepare job application can establish the role record first, or you can supply an equivalent mapping. Missing numerical support is not replaced with an invented accomplishment.

build-roadmap.what: Build roadmaps from one fixed set of branded, interactive components.
build-roadmap.when: A roadmap, timeline, launch plan or delivery plan is needed as a page or inside another page.
build-roadmap.inputs: The work to plan, the governing brand profile, and connected sources when the data lives in a tool.
build-roadmap.outputs: A validated plan JSON rendered as a branded page, an embeddable element or a single-file estate page.
build-roadmap.example: Build a now, next, later roadmap for these initiatives in our confirmed brand.
build-roadmap.expect: It picks a template from its catalog, resolves the brand profile and states it, then writes a plan JSON and builds the roadmap with a script that validates the plan and reports any neutral substitutions and contrast warnings. It uses only confirmed brand values, never ships guessed live-data paths, and never writes back to a source tool.
build-roadmap.requires: Python 3 to run the build script, and a confirmed brand profile if the roadmap should carry one.
build-roadmap.overview: It picks a template from its catalog, resolves the brand profile and states it, then writes a plan JSON and builds the roadmap with a script that validates the plan and reports any neutral substitutions and contrast warnings. It uses only confirmed brand values, never ships guessed live-data paths, and never writes back to a source tool.
build-roadmap.value: Make sequence, timing, dependencies or delivery choices readable in an interactive roadmap. It uses a shared set of components so a timeline embedded in another page behaves consistently with a standalone plan.

preparation.where: Provide initiatives or work items, the intended planning view and any confirmed dates or dependencies. A plan JSON is the structured input the workflow prepares. Brand information is optional; connected sources are needed only if you want it to read data from a tool.
preparation.missing: No existing roadmap file is required. Unknown live-data paths must not be guessed. With no confirmed custom identity it uses neutral styling, and it does not write proposed schedule changes back to the source tool.

estimate-project.what: Estimate a rough effort or cost range.
estimate-project.when: A pursuit needs an early estimate and its basis.
estimate-project.inputs: Supplied scope, comparables, assumptions, and rates when available.
estimate-project.outputs: A sourced estimate range with calculations and reopening conditions.
estimate-project.example: Estimate a rough effort range from these scope items and comparable projects.
estimate-project.expect: It pins the audience, runs the evidence review, then builds a cost and effort range with a basis-of-estimate table where each figure carries its source and confidence. Unconfirmed dimensions show as flagged assumptions, a quote that fails to reconcile is reported with its discrepancy rather than smoothed, and the range is never presented as a quote.
estimate-project.requires: A supplied scope plus a rate card, comparables or an existing quote, and Python 3 for the reconciliation gate.
estimate-project.overview: It pins the audience, runs the evidence review, then builds a cost and effort range with a basis-of-estimate table where each figure carries its source and confidence. Unconfirmed dimensions show as flagged assumptions, a quote that fails to reconcile is reported with its discrepancy rather than smoothed, and the range is never presented as a quote.
estimate-project.value: Give an early effort or cost range with a basis people can inspect and revisit. It is useful before detailed pricing, when uncertainty should remain visible rather than being hidden in a single confident number.

preparation.where: Supply scope and whatever estimate basis exists: comparable projects, rates, assumptions or a quote export. A basis-of-estimate table records where each number comes from and how certain it is; the skill prepares that table.
preparation.missing: Unknown dimensions stay flagged and a non-reconciling quote is reported. A cost range needs a pricing basis. Without one, ask for an effort estimate or identify the missing evidence; the result is not a confirmed quote.

prepare-delivery-handoff.what: Prepare the handoff from sales to delivery.
prepare-delivery-handoff.when: A signed engagement needs a receiving delivery owner.
prepare-delivery-handoff.inputs: The executed agreement, quote, deal record, and receiving team.
prepare-delivery-handoff.outputs: A handoff package with ownership, assumptions, and tracked acceptance.
prepare-delivery-handoff.example: Prepare the sales-to-delivery handoff from the executed agreement and deal record.
prepare-delivery-handoff.expect: It confirms the deal is signed, gathers facts from the executed SOW, quote and deal record, and builds a 12-section handoff manifest that a script gate checks. Every section is filled or carries a named gap with an owner, and it stops with a gap memo if required evidence is insufficient; it never records an acceptance nobody gave.
prepare-delivery-handoff.requires: An executed SOW and its quote for a signed deal, plus Python 3 to run the manifest gate.
prepare-delivery-handoff.overview: It confirms the deal is signed, gathers facts from the executed SOW, quote and deal record, and builds a 12-section handoff manifest that a script gate checks. Every section is filled or carries a named gap with an owner, and it stops with a gap memo if required evidence is insufficient; it never records an acceptance nobody gave.
prepare-delivery-handoff.value: Transfer a sold engagement to a receiving delivery owner with scope, assumptions, decisions and remaining gaps visible. It helps prevent commitments from disappearing between the proposal and kickoff.

preparation.where: Provide the executed SOW, associated quote, deal record and receiving team. An executed SOW is the signed agreement, not a draft. The handoff manifest is the structured package this skill builds for acceptance.
preparation.missing: Required evidence gaps produce a memo with owners rather than an invented complete handoff. If the deal is not signed, this workflow cannot treat it as accepted delivery scope. The receiving owner's acceptance must actually be given.

preparationSkills.reason: Uses the handoff after the receiving owner has accepted it.

review-sales-journey.what: Review a sales journey, demo, or proposed workflow.
review-sales-journey.when: A journey needs specific corrections to steps, systems, or measures.
review-sales-journey.inputs: The journey or demo, customer task, current workflow, and proposed change.
review-sales-journey.outputs: A critique tracing the task and recommending supported corrections.
review-sales-journey.example: Trace this demo against the customer’s task and recommend specific workflow corrections.
review-sales-journey.expect: It reads the artifact and its source evidence first, then checks five things: customer flow, current versus future state, systems, click paths and measures. It returns a prioritized critique with the first repair to make, and it stops before any purchase, submission, message or live record change unless you authorize it.
review-sales-journey.overview: It reads the artifact and its source evidence first, then checks five things: customer flow, current versus future state, systems, click paths and measures. It returns a prioritized critique with the first repair to make, and it stops before any purchase, submission, message or live record change unless you authorize it.
review-sales-journey.value: Test whether a sales demo or proposed workflow helps the customer complete the intended task. It follows the current and proposed steps, systems, clicks and measures to recommend the most useful repair first.

preparation.where: Supply the demo, journey document or workflow and its supporting source material. Explain the customer's task and what happens today; that baseline can be notes, a recording transcript, screenshots or a documented process.
preparation.missing: When the current state is absent, the comparison must identify that gap. It can critique what is visible, but cannot invent clicks, system behavior or improvement measures. A review does not authorize changing live records or sending messages.

map-sales-process.what: Map a sales process from its source files.
map-sales-process.when: Ownership, triggers, handoffs, or systems of record need clarification.
map-sales-process.inputs: Discovery files, workbooks, CRM or Jira exports, and operating notes.
map-sales-process.outputs: A process explanation, diagram, ownership tables, and unresolved questions.
map-sales-process.example: Map the sales process from these files. Identify owners, triggers, handoffs, systems of record, and unresolved questions.
map-sales-process.expect: It inventories your files and exports, reads them completely, and maps each process from trigger to completion with owners, handoffs, record grain and system of record, plus territory and opportunity ownership when relevant. Gaps stay as open questions with locators rather than guessed rules, and it will not change CRM records, territories or Jira issues.
map-sales-process.overview: It reads the supplied notes, workbooks and exports to reconstruct each process from its trigger to completion. It identifies the people involved, handoffs, record grain and authoritative system for each business record, including territory and opportunity ownership where relevant. It produces an explanation, diagram and ownership tables with source-linked questions wherever the evidence does not establish a rule.
map-sales-process.value: Reconstruct who does what from the event that starts a sales process through its handoffs and completion. It explains which system owns each record so territory or opportunity rules do not become disconnected boxes on a diagram.

preparation.where: Provide discovery notes, operating instructions, workbooks or CRM/Jira exports. A system of record is the authoritative system for a particular business record. You need not have a process diagram; producing the explanation, diagram and ownership tables is the task.
preparation.missing: Incomplete sources yield explicit open questions with source locators. Missing ownership, record grain or territory rules must not be guessed. Files and exports are enough to begin; no live CRM connection is required for mapping them.

compare-scope-options.what: Compare scope options in a static document.
compare-scope-options.when: A printable scope summary or option matrix is needed.
compare-scope-options.inputs: One versioned quote or export with scope, hours, staffing, price, and timeline.
compare-scope-options.outputs: A reconciled scope summary or side-by-side option comparison.
compare-scope-options.example: Create a printable comparison of these options from one confirmed quote revision.
compare-scope-options.expect: It asks for the client, quote IDs and order, then needs either a quote connector or a dated quote export. It reconciles every scope item, hour value, status and staffing-snapshot price with a validator before building a self-contained HTML page, and it stops the build if no real scope records are supplied.
compare-scope-options.requires: A current quote connection or a dated quote export, and Python 3 for the validator and builder.
compare-scope-options.overview: It asks for the client, quote IDs and order, then needs either a quote connector or a dated quote export. It reconciles every scope item, hour value, status and staffing-snapshot price with a validator before building a self-contained HTML page, and it stops the build if no real scope records are supplied.
compare-scope-options.value: Give a buyer or approver a printable comparison whose inclusions, staffing and price all come from the same quote revision. It makes differences between options visible without an interactive proposal page.

preparation.where: Provide the quote identifiers and dated exports with real scope items, hours, staffing and prices, or a supported quote connection. A staffing snapshot is the role/rate information used in that quote, not today's rate card substituted afterward.
preparation.missing: With no real scope records the build stops. An export can replace a connector; a quote number alone cannot replace the underlying data. Discrepancies need resolution rather than adjustments made only for presentation.

scope-project.what: Develop scope, effort, staffing, and timeline estimates.
scope-project.when: A project needs a rough range or a confirmed quote revision.
scope-project.inputs: The brief, scope model, comparables, rate card, and relevant constraints.
scope-project.outputs: Scope items and estimates with shown calculations. Unknown effort remains visible as unestimated. Staffing and schedule bounds follow the supplied capacity and dependencies.
scope-project.example: Estimate effort, staffing, and timing for this scope using the supplied rate card.
scope-project.expect: It reads your brief first, then builds scope items with sources and acceptance conditions and, when asked, a low, expected and high effort range from a local calculator. Work with no effort basis stays unestimated, totals are marked incomplete, and it changes a quote record only inside an authorized request.
scope-project.requires: Python 3 for the local estimate calculator, plus a rate card or confirmed quote if you want a cost figure.
scope-project.overview: It reads your brief first, then builds scope items with sources and acceptance conditions and, when asked, a low, expected and high effort range from a local calculator. Work with no effort basis stays unestimated, totals are marked incomplete, and it changes a quote record only inside an authorized request.
scope-project.value: Break a proposed engagement into scope items and estimate effort, staffing and timing from stated assumptions. It keeps unestimated work visible so an apparently complete total does not conceal unknowns.

preparation.where: Bring the brief, constraints and available comparable work. Supply a rate card or confirmed quote if a cost is required. The scope model is the structured list this skill develops; a CRM connector is optional when you provide exports or a local quote model.
preparation.missing: It can begin with the brief. Items with no effort basis remain unestimated and totals are labeled incomplete. Without capacity and dependencies, schedule bounds cannot be treated as a committed delivery date.

prepare-session-handoff.what: Prepare another session to resume the same work.
prepare-session-handoff.when: The current session is ending or needs a handoff.
prepare-session-handoff.inputs: The session’s decisions, files, running state, and completed checks.
prepare-session-handoff.outputs: A handoff with the current state, verification, open questions, and exact next action.
prepare-session-handoff.example: Prepare a handoff with the current files, decisions, verification, and exact next action.
prepare-session-handoff.expect: It stamps the time, directory and git state once, then writes a fixed-template handoff from what happened in the session, with absolute paths and 'none' for empty sections. It prints the handoff in chat and saves a file only where a handoffs directory already exists, and it does not audit the filesystem or update memory.
prepare-session-handoff.overview: It stamps the time, directory and git state once, then writes a fixed-template handoff from what happened in the session, with absolute paths and 'none' for empty sections. It prints the handoff in chat and saves a file only where a handoffs directory already exists, and it does not audit the filesystem or update memory.
prepare-session-handoff.value: Give a fresh session the decisions, current files, verification state and next action it needs to resume. It helps preserve working context without requiring the next agent to reconstruct the entire conversation.

preparation.where: Use it in the session that did the work, or supply a reliable session record. File paths, Git state, commands and unresolved questions come from that work; no separate handoff document is required beforehand.
preparation.missing: It cannot reconstruct missing history by assumption. It prints the handoff in chat and saves only to an existing handoffs directory. This workflow does not perform an unrelated filesystem audit or update memory.

configure-salesforce-project.what: Install, audit or repair a Salesforce repository's delivery standards.
configure-salesforce-project.when: A project needs its hooks, instruction contract, tracker or trunk settings set up, checked or fixed.
configure-salesforce-project.inputs: The repository, its delivery mode, tracker, host and ownership mode, and authenticated prerequisites.
configure-salesforce-project.outputs: Installed or repaired hooks and contract blocks, recorded configuration, and an audit result for each piece.
configure-salesforce-project.example: Audit this Salesforce repository's delivery hooks and project instructions, and fix what is no longer armed.
configure-salesforce-project.expect: It runs a prerequisites check first, asks only for settings it cannot detect (tracker, trunk branch, platform), then installs hooks and a managed instruction block, audits what it installed and prints a client-conversation checklist. It never accepts a pasted credential, directing you to the browser login commands instead, and the audit is read-only unless you add --fix.
configure-salesforce-project.overview: It runs a prerequisites check first, asks only for settings it cannot detect (tracker, trunk branch, platform), then installs hooks and a managed instruction block, audits what it installed and prints a client-conversation checklist. It never accepts a pasted credential, directing you to the browser login commands instead, and the audit is read-only unless you add --fix.
configure-salesforce-project.value: Set up or audit the repository checks and project instructions that govern Salesforce delivery. It connects hooks, tracker conventions and the chosen delivery mode, then checks that the installed pieces are actually armed.

preparation.where: Provide the repository and its intended tracker, trunk branch, host and ownership mode. Existing hooks and configuration are inspected first. Authentication must already be available through supported login methods; this skill does not supply credentials or a Salesforce org.
preparation.missing: Missing prerequisites or undetectable settings must be resolved before installation. A plain audit is read-only; a requested repair follows the fix path. This setup skill is separate from applying code architecture or deploying a feature.

operate-salesforce-pipeline.what: Operate an existing sf-deploy-engine Salesforce pipeline.
operate-salesforce-pipeline.when: A pipeline environment needs status, promotion, a release, rollback, revalidation or freeze recovery.
operate-salesforce-pipeline.inputs: The repository's pipeline.yml, a privately stored engine token and the authorized tickets or SHAs.
operate-salesforce-pipeline.outputs: Engine status and the verified result of the requested operation.
operate-salesforce-pipeline.example: Check the engine's status and release GH-397 from preprod to main.
operate-salesforce-pipeline.expect: It works from the repo's pipeline.yml and reports status, promotes, cuts releases, rolls back by ticket or SHA, or runs a read-only doctor check. It refuses to run a manual sf deploy against a pipeline environment's org, and it states that its guards stop an agent in this session, not a person deploying from a terminal.
operate-salesforce-pipeline.overview: It works from the repo's pipeline.yml and reports status, promotes, cuts releases, rolls back by ticket or SHA, or runs a read-only doctor check. It refuses to run a manual sf deploy against a pipeline environment's org, and it states that its guards stop an agent in this session, not a person deploying from a terminal.
operate-salesforce-pipeline.value: Use an already configured sf-deploy-engine pipeline for status, promotion, releases, rollback and diagnosis. It preserves the pipeline's own release controls instead of treating deployment as an arbitrary CLI push.

preparation.where: Supply the repository containing pipeline.yml and the tickets or commit SHAs for the requested operation. pipeline.yml describes this project's environments. The engine token is a privately stored credential configured outside chat, not a value to paste into the request.
preparation.missing: If the pipeline or token is absent, the existing-pipeline workflow cannot operate it. It does not create a new pipeline automatically or substitute a manual deploy against a managed pipeline org.

apply-salesforce-patterns.what: Apply the estate Salesforce architecture and check code against it.
apply-salesforce-patterns.when: Apex, trigger or LWC work in a project that uses service, selector and unit-of-work conventions.
apply-salesforce-patterns.inputs: The codebase, its architecture decisions and the requested feature or review.
apply-salesforce-patterns.outputs: For a new feature, Apex and LWC code organized around the adopted layers, plus architecture-check results. For an existing-code review, specific violations, proposed corrections and design findings that require judgment beyond the checker.
apply-salesforce-patterns.example: Review this Apex change against the project's service, selector and unit-of-work patterns.
apply-salesforce-patterns.expect: It reads your project's architecture decisions first, then structures Apex and LWC into trigger, service, selector, unit-of-work and controller layers and runs arch_check.py. The checker exits 1 on a blocking violation, suppressions need a stated reason, and if adoption is undecided it reports findings and leaves enforcement uninstalled.
apply-salesforce-patterns.overview: It structures Salesforce code around shared business services: triggers, screens and APIs call the same business logic; selectors contain database queries; a Unit of Work groups record writes; and controllers connect the interface to the services. For existing code it runs the bundled architecture checker, then reviews design issues the checker cannot judge, such as unclear transaction ownership or business logic hidden in controllers. It checks the project's existing conventions before proposing adoption.
apply-salesforce-patterns.value: Keep business rules consistent when the same record change comes from a screen, trigger or API. For example, those entry points can call one service instead of maintaining separate versions of an opportunity rule.

preparation.where: Provide the Salesforce repository or relevant Apex/LWC files. Project architecture means the existing code organization and agreed design choices: look in README, architecture notes, decision records and nearby code. No document with a specific name is required, and no separate architecture skill is required first.
preparation.missing: If there are no documented decisions, the skill can report compatibility with its bundled reference pattern and leave adoption for you to decide. It preserves established conventions and leaves enforcement uninstalled while adoption is undecided. Python runs the checker; PMD is optional because a fallback engine exists.

preparationSkills.reason: Optional help for an unresolved design; not a required step before reviewing existing code.

capture-salesforce-screens.what: Capture Salesforce UI evidence and run clickpath checks.
capture-salesforce-screens.when: An authorized UI path needs screenshots or assertions.
capture-salesforce-screens.inputs: The org connection, supported screenshot runtime, and target path.
capture-salesforce-screens.outputs: Screenshots, clickpath results, and observed UI issues.
capture-salesforce-screens.example: Capture this Salesforce clickpath and check its stated acceptance conditions.
capture-salesforce-screens.expect: It needs a confirmed org alias and a page or record, and checks that the selected sfqa tool exists before running anything. It captures screenshots or runs clickpath assertions and reports a screenshot as not ready if a load stage timed out; if no supported tool or browser is available, it reports the check as pending rather than improvising.
capture-salesforce-screens.overview: It needs a confirmed org alias and a page or record, and checks that the selected sfqa tool exists before running anything. It captures screenshots or runs clickpath assertions and reports a screenshot as not ready if a load stage timed out; if no supported tool or browser is available, it reports the check as pending rather than improvising.
capture-salesforce-screens.value: Show what an authorized Salesforce click path actually renders and where an asserted step fails. Screenshots and click-path results support review of the running interface rather than an assumption based on code.

preparation.where: Provide the confirmed org alias and the target page, record or acceptance path. The environment must have the supported sfqa tool or an authorized browser runtime; these are execution capabilities, not another document to author.
preparation.missing: Without a supported tool or browser, the UI check remains pending. A timed-out load is not a ready screenshot. Org authentication and the intended target must be confirmed before accessing the interface.

deliver-salesforce-change.what: Deliver a change to a single-org Salesforce project.
deliver-salesforce-change.when: An authorized Salesforce change needs the project delivery workflow.
deliver-salesforce-change.inputs: The issue, repository, target org, configuration, and requested change.
deliver-salesforce-change.outputs: The change with separate validation, review, deployment, and acceptance evidence.
deliver-salesforce-change.example: Prepare this authorized Salesforce change using the project’s isolated delivery workflow.
deliver-salesforce-change.expect: It requires a GitHub issue first, then works in an isolated worktree with local checks, a per-commit dry run against a confirmed org, a squash merge and a deploy from main. With no org it stops at 'prepared locally' and never records a validation or deployment as done, and it counts the task finished only when the ticket is closed and the worktree removed.
deliver-salesforce-change.overview: It requires a GitHub issue first, then works in an isolated worktree with local checks, a per-commit dry run against a confirmed org, a squash merge and a deploy from main. With no org it stops at 'prepared locally' and never records a validation or deployment as done, and it counts the task finished only when the ticket is closed and the worktree removed.
deliver-salesforce-change.value: Carry a Salesforce issue through isolated implementation, checks, validation and the project's merge/deployment process. It keeps evidence for each delivery stage instead of equating a code change with an accepted result.

preparation.where: Provide the GitHub issue, repository, configured delivery process and confirmed target org. The issue defines the requested change; project instructions and configuration define the delivery steps. Verify Salesforce org is a bundled target-identity helper.
preparation.missing: A GitHub issue is required to start this workflow. With no org access the change can only be prepared locally; validation and deployment stay unperformed. Missing acceptance or ticket closure prevents a claim of full delivery completion.

preparationSkills.reason: Sets up the project delivery stack if it is not configured.
Checks the target identity before an authorized Salesforce write.

author-estate-skill.what: Create or repair a workflow for the Skills Estate.
author-estate-skill.when: An estate addition, collision review or behavioral repair.
author-estate-skill.inputs: The recurring task, example requests, source methods, and expected outputs.
author-estate-skill.outputs: The preserved workflow, governed intake, metadata, required resources and validation evidence.
author-estate-skill.example: Create a focused skill from this repeated workflow and these example requests.
author-estate-skill.expect: It first checks the closest existing skills and asks whether the task belongs in a skill at all, then records a collision decision and intake before scaffolding a draft outside the installed set. It tests a positive, an alternate and a nearby negative request, and creating a draft never installs it.
author-estate-skill.requires: A Skills Estate checkout and Python 3 for the scaffolder and checks.
author-estate-skill.overview: It first checks the closest existing skills and asks whether the task belongs in a skill at all, then records a collision decision and intake before scaffolding a draft outside the installed set. It tests a positive, an alternate and a nearby negative request, and creating a draft never installs it.
author-estate-skill.value: Turn a repeated workflow into a skill with a clear trigger, useful resources and checks that distinguish it from neighboring skills. It first tests whether an existing skill or mode already covers the job.

preparation.where: Bring representative requests, the source method, expected outputs and known failure cases. The intake records the design and overlap decision; the scaffolder creates the draft. Both are tools in the estate checkout rather than forms you must already have completed.
preparation.missing: Without an estate checkout the governed scaffolder cannot run. Missing examples or unclear task boundaries need clarification before treating the draft as tested. This mode is included in Maintain skills estate; creating a draft does not install it.

preparationSkills.reason: Owns the maintenance package containing this authoring mode.

maintain-skills-estate.what: Maintain a Skills Estate checkout by authoring, validating, packaging and releasing workflows.
maintain-skills-estate.when: A workflow needs creating or repair, packages need building, a reviewed release needs installing, or another host needs an update.
maintain-skills-estate.inputs: The canonical estate checkout, the reviewed source hash for installation and the target host.
maintain-skills-estate.outputs: Validation and build results, packages, installation receipts and publication records for the requested operation.
maintain-skills-estate.example: Validate the current estate and build candidate packages without installing them.
maintain-skills-estate.expect: It works only on the confirmed estate checkout and runs the single operation you ask for, such as validate, build, bundle, status or install. Install needs the exact reviewed source hash, refuses to overwrite a divergent installation, and a successful build is reported as packaging only, not proof the skill works.
maintain-skills-estate.overview: It runs the requested maintenance operation on a confirmed estate checkout: author or repair a workflow, validate source, assemble complete packages, inspect drift, install a reviewed release or replace a package on another host. Installation uses the exact reviewed source hash and protects divergent files with conflict checks and rollback records. A successful build establishes packaging, not runtime acceptance.
maintain-skills-estate.value: Keep authored workflows, complete packages and reviewed installations distinguishable as the estate changes. It can validate or build without installation, or install a specified reviewed version with conflict checks and rollback records.

preparation.where: Use the confirmed Skills Estate repository or the configured repository pointer. The reviewed source hash identifies the exact accepted content for an installation; validate/build operations do not require an installation approval. Python and the repository's declared runtimes must be available.
preparation.missing: Without a checkout it cannot synchronize an estate. Divergent installations are reported rather than overwritten. Missing review evidence prevents promotion even when a package builds; another host's account upload remains a separate operation.

assess-solution-delivery.what: Decide whether a proposed client solution can be delivered and make its delivery logic inspectable.
assess-solution-delivery.when: A solution needs deal approval, a build reference for developers or a field guide for a scoping call.
assess-solution-delivery.inputs: A validated evidence ledger and gate report, plus the systems, interfaces, scope, staffing and commercial baseline.
assess-solution-delivery.outputs: A validated solution graph rendered as a Solution Brief, build reference or field guide, or a Technical Readiness Memo when evidence is insufficient.
assess-solution-delivery.example: Explain whether this solution can be delivered, including systems, interfaces, risks and decisions.
assess-solution-delivery.expect: It starts from a validated evidence ledger and gate report, then judges whether the solution is deliverable and builds a graph that a script validates before any page is drafted. If the evidence gate is Insufficient it stops at a short Technical Readiness Memo, and it does not approve margin, rates or commercial terms.
assess-solution-delivery.requires: A validated evidence ledger and gate report from the evidence-core step, and Python 3; field guide mode also needs Node.js and Playwright for its browser check.
assess-solution-delivery.overview: It checks the evidence for the proposed solution, then connects systems, interfaces, scope, ownership, staffing assumptions and risks in a structured solution graph. A validator checks that graph before it is rendered as a Solution Brief, build reference or scoping field guide. Insufficient evidence produces a Technical Readiness Memo identifying what prevents a delivery judgment.
assess-solution-delivery.value: Determine whether a proposed solution has a defensible delivery path across its systems, interfaces, scope, people and risks. It gives approvers or developers a connected explanation rather than a list of components.

preparation.where: Bring system and interface evidence, scoped work, constraints and commercial/staffing context. Evidence core creates the source-and-claim ledger and its gate report. The solution graph is the structured relationship model this workflow prepares; you need not draw it first.
preparation.missing: If the evidence gate is insufficient, it returns a Technical Readiness Memo identifying what prevents a delivery judgment. A proposal can be explored, but absent evidence cannot be converted into an approved architecture or commercial decision.

preparationSkills.reason: Prepares the evidence ledger and gate report this workflow requires.

write-statement-of-work.what: Draft a statement of work from confirmed scope.
write-statement-of-work.when: A fixed-scope, adaptive, or assessment agreement needs drafting.
write-statement-of-work.inputs: The confirmed quote model and the project’s approved contract and brand profiles.
write-statement-of-work.outputs: A reconciled Word document and checks against the selected scope and terms.
write-statement-of-work.example: Draft the selected SOW variant from this confirmed quote and approved contract profile.
write-statement-of-work.expect: It reads one confirmed quote revision, picks the SOW variant from the engagement shape, and renders a .docx only after the hours and revenue tie out. A figure that does not reconcile stops the build and is returned to the quote owner, missing values stay visible as flagged fields, and the document is never treated as approved or sent.
write-statement-of-work.overview: It reads one confirmed quote revision, picks the SOW variant from the engagement shape, and renders a .docx only after the hours and revenue tie out. A figure that does not reconcile stops the build and is returned to the quote owner, missing values stay visible as flagged fields, and the document is never treated as approved or sent.
write-statement-of-work.value: Translate an agreed quote into a consistent statement of work with scope, obligations and commercial figures tied together. It checks hours and revenue before rendering the Word document.

preparation.where: Provide one confirmed quote revision and the project's approved contract profile. The profile is the authorized clause/template set and contract choices, supplied by the agreement owner; no former employer's terms are assumed. A brand profile controls appearance and can use neutral defaults.
preparation.missing: Missing approved terms or unreconciled figures prevent a complete contract build. Unknown values remain visible rather than invented. A draft document is not legal approval, acceptance, signature or delivery to the client.

review-contract-scope.what: Review a statement of work and its obligations.
review-contract-scope.when: A SOW or contractual scope needs a quality review.
review-contract-scope.inputs: The draft agreement, confirmed scope, estimate, and controlling terms.
review-contract-scope.outputs: Findings or revisions addressing ambiguity, duplication, and scope consistency.
review-contract-scope.example: Review this SOW for ambiguous obligations and inconsistencies with the agreed scope.
review-contract-scope.expect: It reads the whole SOW with its quote and template, runs a scan for repeated mechanics, then fixes structure and cross-references and re-scans. It flags numbers that do not trace to the pricing source instead of changing them, and the edited document stays unapproved.
review-contract-scope.requires: The SOW as a .docx or text with its controlling quote, and Python 3 for the scan script.
review-contract-scope.overview: It reads the whole SOW with its quote and template, runs a scan for repeated mechanics, then fixes structure and cross-references and re-scans. It flags numbers that do not trace to the pricing source instead of changing them, and the edited document stays unapproved.
review-contract-scope.value: Find ambiguous obligations, repeated mechanics and inconsistencies between a SOW and the quote it should represent. It checks document structure and cross-references while retaining the agreed commercial basis.

preparation.where: Supply the complete SOW, its controlling quote and the approved template or terms. A Word file or full text works. The template is the agreement owner's baseline language, not a contract policy generated by this skill.
preparation.missing: Without the quote, numerical consistency cannot be verified. Unsupported figures are flagged rather than changed to fit. The review can repair the document but does not approve or sign the resulting agreement.

specify-implementation.what: Specify detailed UI, API, and data behavior.
specify-implementation.when: A feature specification needs implementation detail.
specify-implementation.inputs: The current implementation, user flows, interfaces, data, and constraints.
specify-implementation.outputs: A detailed specification with states, persistence, interfaces, and acceptance checks.
specify-implementation.example: Specify the UI states, API contracts, and data changes for this feature.
specify-implementation.expect: It reads the project instructions and relevant code first, then writes only the sections the feature needs: states, data changes, endpoints, a file manifest and executable acceptance checks. It keeps planned verification separate from commands that actually ran and does not invent owners, dates or approvals.
specify-implementation.overview: It reads the project instructions and relevant code first, then writes only the sections the feature needs: states, data changes, endpoints, a file manifest and executable acceptance checks. It keeps planned verification separate from commands that actually ran and does not invent owners, dates or approvals.
specify-implementation.value: Make a feature specific enough to build: user flows, loading/error/empty states, data persistence, endpoints and affected files. It is useful when a product-level requirement still leaves engineers to invent behavior.

preparation.where: Provide the feature brief and access to relevant implementation and project instructions. Existing API and data contracts come from the repository or project documents. No particular specification template or prior architecture skill is mandatory.
